bit.name: weight the two neighbouring samples by position along the segment
bit.mechanism: find the two samples that bracket the query, and return the value that lies the same fraction of the way between them as the query lies between their positions
fails_when: kinks at every sample; error grows with curvature

bit.name: copy the value of the nearest sample
bit.mechanism: return the value of whichever sample lies closest to the query; the result is piecewise constant with jumps midway between samples
fails_when: discontinuous; blocky under magnification

bit.name: fit the unique polynomial through all the points
bit.mechanism: through n+1 points there is exactly one polynomial of degree at most n; construct it (by a basis of products that vanish at all other points, or by solving for coefficients) and evaluate it at the query
fails_when: wild oscillation between equally spaced points as the degree grows

bit.name: build each higher-degree interpolant from a pair of lower-degree ones
bit.mechanism: start with the sample values as degree-zero interpolants; combine each adjacent pair into the degree-one interpolant at the query point by a position-weighted blend, then pairs of those into degree two, and so on up a triangular tableau to a single value
fails_when: one query per tableau; quadratic work

bit.name: fit a polynomial matching both values and derivatives at the points
bit.mechanism: raise the degree so that at each sample the polynomial matches not only the value but also the first few derivatives; each matched derivative is one more linear condition on the coefficients
fails_when: needs derivatives that measured data rarely provides

bit.name: join low-degree pieces with matching derivatives at the knots
bit.mechanism: use a separate low-degree polynomial on each interval between samples, and choose their coefficients so that values and the first few derivatives agree where pieces meet; smoothness comes from the joins, not from a high degree
fails_when: overshoot near steep data; a change in one sample moves the whole curve (for natural splines)

bit.name: clamp the slopes at the knots so every piece stays monotone
bit.mechanism: estimate a slope at each knot from its neighbours, then limit each slope (to zero at local extremes, and to a bound from the adjacent secants elsewhere) so that no cubic piece can overshoot between two increasing or two decreasing samples
fails_when: loses one order of accuracy where slopes are clamped

bit.name: repeatedly blend adjacent control points at the parameter until one remains
bit.mechanism: replace each adjacent pair of control points by their weighted average at the parameter value (weights from the knot positions), then repeat on the shorter list until a single point remains; that point is the curve value, and only convex combinations are ever formed
requires: control points and (for the general form) a knot vector
fails_when: quadratic in the degree per evaluation

bit.name: convolve the samples with a windowed sinc kernel
bit.mechanism: each output value is a weighted sum of the nearby input samples, the weights being an ideal reconstruction kernel (sinc) multiplied by a window that cuts it off after a few lobes; the window trades ringing against blur
fails_when: ringing near edges; not monotone

bit.name: multiply by the matrix repeatedly and renormalise
bit.mechanism: apply the matrix to a vector, rescale to unit length, and repeat; the component along the dominant eigenvector grows fastest, so the vector converges to it and the growth factor to its eigenvalue
fails_when: slow when the two largest eigenvalues are close; finds only the dominant one

bit.name: repeatedly solve with a shifted matrix to amplify the eigenvector nearest the shift
bit.mechanism: instead of multiplying by the matrix, solve a linear system with the matrix minus a chosen shift each round; the eigenvalue closest to the shift becomes the dominant one of the inverse, so the vector converges to its eigenvector
requires: a shift near the wanted eigenvalue (policy)
fails_when: each round costs a solve; a shift exactly on an eigenvalue is singular

bit.name: move the shift to the current quotient each round
bit.mechanism: run the shifted-solve iteration but, after each round, replace the shift by the current vector's own estimate of its eigenvalue (the quotient of the two inner products); convergence becomes cubic near a solution
fails_when: which eigenvalue it finds depends on the start

bit.name: factor into orthogonal times triangular, remultiply in reverse order, repeat
bit.mechanism: factor the matrix as an orthogonal factor times an upper-triangular factor, multiply them back in the opposite order to get a similar matrix, and repeat; the sub-diagonal decays and the eigenvalues appear on the diagonal (shifts and deflation accelerate it)
fails_when: cubic per iteration without a preliminary reduction to compact form

bit.name: rotate in a plane to zero the largest off-diagonal entry, repeatedly
bit.mechanism: pick the largest off-diagonal element of a symmetric matrix, apply the plane rotation that makes it zero (touching only its two rows and columns), and repeat; the sum of squared off-diagonals falls every step and the diagonal converges to the eigenvalues
fails_when: zeroed entries refill; many sweeps

entry: Krylov methods (for large sparse matrix problems; third most-important numerical method class of the 20th century as ran

bit.name: solve within the span of successive matrix powers of a vector
bit.mechanism: build the subspace spanned by a vector, the matrix times it, the matrix squared times it, and so on, using only matrix-vector products; project the problem onto that growing subspace and solve the small projected problem, whose solution converges to the true one long before the subspace fills the space
requires: a matrix-vector product only (matrix need not be stored)
fails_when: the raw powers become nearly parallel; an orthogonalisation step is needed in practice

bit.name: subtract the projections onto the previous vectors, then normalise
bit.mechanism: take the vectors in order; from each, subtract its projection onto every vector already processed so that what remains is perpendicular to all of them, then scale it to unit length; the spans are preserved at every prefix
fails_when: orthogonality is lost in floating point unless the subtraction is done one vector at a time (the modified form)

bit.name: shift blocks around a torus so each node always multiplies a matching pair
bit.mechanism: lay both matrices out in blocks on a square grid of nodes, skew the rows of one and the columns of the other so that every node holds a pair whose product belongs to it, multiply and accumulate, then shift one matrix left and the other up by one node and repeat for as many rounds as the grid is wide
requires: a square node grid with wrap-around neighbours
memory for one block of each operand per node
fails_when: non-square grids or non-divisible sizes

bit.name: compare both sides applied to a random vector
bit.mechanism: to check a claimed product, draw a random vector, multiply the claimed result by it and multiply the two factors by it in sequence, and compare; a wrong claim survives with probability at most one half per trial, and the check costs only matrix-vector products
fails_when: one-sided: it never rejects a correct claim, but can accept a wrong one

bit.name: eliminate each variable below its pivot, then back-substitute
bit.mechanism: for each column in turn, subtract multiples of the pivot row from the rows below so that column is zero beneath the pivot; the system becomes triangular and is solved from the last variable upward
requires: a nonzero pivot (row swaps supply one)
fails_when: small pivots amplify rounding; cubic cost; fill-in destroys sparsity

bit.name: update each variable in turn from the latest values of the others
bit.mechanism: sweep through the equations; solve each for its own variable using the most recent values of all the others (including those updated earlier in the same sweep), and repeat sweeps until the changes are small
requires: diagonal dominance or a similar condition for convergence
fails_when: diverges on many matrices; inherently sequential within a sweep

bit.name: overshoot each update by a fixed relaxation factor
bit.mechanism: wherever an iteration would move a variable to a new value, move it further along the same direction by a fixed factor greater than one (or less than one to damp); the right factor can cut the number of sweeps by an order of magnitude
fails_when: a factor at or beyond 2 diverges; the best factor is problem-dependent

bit.name: extend the solution one order at a time using the shift structure
bit.mechanism: for a matrix whose entries depend only on the difference of their indices, the solution of the order-n system is obtained from the order-(n-1) solution and its reversal by one inner product and one scaling, so the whole solve costs a square rather than a cube
fails_when: numerically weaker than elimination on ill-conditioned inputs

bit.name: iterate corrections through an incomplete factorisation that keeps the sparsity pattern
bit.mechanism: factor the sparse matrix approximately into lower and upper triangular factors that are forced to keep the original sparsity pattern (the mismatch is chosen to partly cancel), then repeatedly solve for a correction to the residual through these cheap factors
fails_when: convergence depends on the parameter; not general-purpose

bit.name: prune dominated columns, then recurse on the even rows to find all row maxima
bit.mechanism: in a matrix whose row-maximum positions never move left as you go down, first delete columns that can hold no row maximum (a stack pass comparing adjacent columns), then solve recursively on the even rows and fill the odd rows by scanning only between their neighbours' answers; total work linear in the dimensions
fails_when: the monotonicity condition is the whole assumption; it is not checked

bit.name: number vertices by breadth-first levels from a peripheral start
bit.mechanism: start at a vertex of low degree far from the centre, visit the graph level by level breadth-first (neighbours in increasing degree), and number the vertices in visiting order (reversing the order at the end); connected vertices then have nearby numbers so the matrix nonzeros hug the diagonal
fails_when: a bad starting vertex gives a wide band

bit.name: eliminate the vertex of smallest degree first
bit.mechanism: repeatedly pick the vertex with the fewest current neighbours, eliminate it (its neighbours become mutually connected, which is exactly the fill that factorisation would create), and record the order; the ordering keeps the fill small
fails_when: greedy; no optimality guarantee (the exact problem is hard)

bit.name: compute the fill pattern before the numeric factorisation
bit.mechanism: using only which entries are nonzero, simulate the factorisation on the graph to find every position that will become nonzero, allocate exactly that storage, and then run the numeric factorisation into the preallocated pattern with no dynamic growth
fails_when: pivoting for stability changes the pattern and invalidates it

bit.name: propose a move and accept it with probability given by the density ratio
bit.mechanism: from the current point draw a proposal; accept it with probability equal to the ratio of the target density at the proposal to that at the current point (corrected for an asymmetric proposal), capped at one, otherwise stay; the sequence of points has the target as its long-run distribution
requires: the target density up to a constant
fails_when: slow mixing between separated modes; correlated samples

bit.name: redraw one variable from its conditional given the rest
bit.mechanism: cycle through the variables; replace each in turn by a fresh draw from its distribution conditioned on the current values of all the others; every such move is accepted, and the joint sequence converges to the target
requires: a samplable conditional for every variable
fails_when: strongly coupled variables move very slowly

bit.name: propose by simulating momentum dynamics, then accept or reject
bit.mechanism: give the current point a random momentum, simulate frictionless motion under the potential given by the negative log density for a fixed time with a reversible integrator, and accept the endpoint by the usual ratio test on the total energy; long coherent moves replace random-walk steps
requires: a gradient of the log density
a reversible integrator and a step length (policy)
fails_when: discrete variables; step-length tuning

bit.name: penalise revisited levels to flatten the visit histogram
bit.mechanism: keep a running estimate of how many states share each energy level; accept moves by the ratio of those estimates so frequently visited levels become less attractive, multiply the estimate of every visited level by a factor, and shrink the factor each time the visit histogram is flat; the estimate converges to the true density of states
fails_when: the modification factor saturates the error; flatness tests are heuristic

bit.name: split the region where the variance is largest and allocate samples in proportion
bit.mechanism: spend a few samples estimating the variance of the integrand in each half of the region along each axis, split along the axis that most reduces total variance, give each half a share of the remaining samples proportional to its estimated spread, and recurse until the budget is small
requires: a minimum sample budget per leaf (policy)
fails_when: variance estimates from few samples misdirect the split

bit.name: halve the bracket, keeping the half with the sign change
bit.mechanism: given two points where the function has opposite signs, evaluate at the midpoint and keep whichever half still changes sign; the bracket halves every step, so the error is known exactly in advance
requires: a continuous function and an initial sign change
fails_when: one bit per evaluation; cannot find roots without a sign change (even multiplicity)

bit.name: step to the zero of the chord across the bracket, keeping the sign change
bit.mechanism: draw the straight line between the two bracket endpoints and take its zero as the new point; replace whichever endpoint has the same sign, so the bracket is never lost; a stale endpoint is handled by halving its weight (the Illinois modification)
fails_when: one endpoint can stick for many steps without the weighting fix

bit.name: step to the zero of a model fitted through the last few points
bit.mechanism: fit a simple model (a line through the last two points, a parabola or an exponential through the last three) and take its zero as the next point; no derivative is needed and convergence is superlinear, but no bracket is kept
fails_when: divergence when the model is poor; complex iterates for the parabola form

bit.name: step to the zero of the local second-order rational model
bit.mechanism: use the value, first and second derivative at the current point to fit a hyperbola (a rational function of degree one over one) tangent to the function, and jump to its zero; the error cubes each step near a simple root
fails_when: the second derivative is often unavailable or expensive

bit.name: project the interpolated step into a shrinking bisection window
bit.mechanism: compute the chord's zero, nudge it toward the midpoint by a controlled amount, then clip it into a window around the midpoint whose width shrinks so that the worst case still halves the bracket like bisection; on smooth functions the clipped step is the fast one
fails_when: nothing in the worst case beyond bisection; constants matter for the average case
